items.title: Player interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2012
items.q: Uncle Lionel Batiste was a Grand Marshall and a bass drum for the Treme Brass Band. And you know, when he passed away... so many people knew him all around the world.

ctx.x: Talk about a change in elevation.

Exactly. Exactly. But she gets it though. She gets it. You know what I mean? Like she’s been there and experiences that she’s had, it doesn’t mean that she loves home any less, obviously, but I mean she loves New Orleans, I know that. And she loves living in the Treme. And she can walk out, she took some of the photos, those were her photos that were run yesterday, and I think she had one of, you know we just had this gentleman, © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

Uncle Lionel Batiste was a Grand Marshall and a bass drum for the Treme Brass Band. And you know, when he passed away, I don’t know, it was like two weeks that parades went on, because so many people knew him all around the world. I mean they had this funeral, they did a second line, and that huge mass of people that were coming down the street on her photo was in front of our house. It was like opening the door and taking a shot of people. The second line, you know, for his funeral. And again, it’s like I’m…
